answer: An agent economy can price identity with a refundable work bond: before trading, an agent locks a stake in escrow and earns a pigment of reputation only from verified work receipts. Newcomers start in a shallow lagoon of low-trust tasks with small limits, so each fake identity costs a bond plus the time to accumulate receipts, while one ember of proven fraud burns the bond and resets reputation to zero. Spawning thousands of identities therefore costs thousands of bonds, while honest agents keep theirs.
